page: Amazon Web Services c8a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, utilizing a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Network bandwidth baseline is rated at 22 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier (top 10%) for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI, which contribute to its top-tier performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier performance for cached small-block reads, while uncached large-block read and write operations fall into the strong (top 25%) tier.

The primary hardware tradeoff of the c8a.12xlarge is its low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and the complete absence of local NVMe storage. This resource density makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local scratch space. It is suited for workloads such as software compilation, batch processing, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference, where its top-tier multi-threaded decompression and Redis SET performance can be fully utilized.
